henry.title: Rover Rules: Fractions, Division, and an Unknown
henry.intro: A 15-minute math lab. The story is a rover mission, but every number is a pretend model made up for practice. These are not Regolith readings and not NASA measurements. Your score is problems 1–3 on the worksheet.
steps: 📖 Read the three short chunks. Tap 🔊 if you want. Answer each check.
👀 Study the worked example on the worksheet. It is already solved.
🧮 Solve problems 1, 2, and 3. Show your work. This is the assignment.
🏅 Challenge only if you finish and want more. It is not required.

passage.text: 🔢 Every number today is a pretend model. It was made up for math. It is not a distance, fuel, or speed from the game, and it is not a NASA fact.
passage.a: No. They are pretend model numbers.

passage.text: 🍕 A fraction names part of one whole. To add 1/2 and 1/3, use sixths: 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6, so 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.

⚖️ An equation says both sides are equal. The letter is an unknown. Inverse operations undo each other: division undoes multiplication, and subtraction undoes addition. Example: 20 = 4 × t, so t = 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Check: 4 × 5 = 20.

words: numbers made up for this math, not a measurement
a part of one whole, such as 3/4
the result of a division, not counting the leftover
the leftover after making equal groups
a statement that two sides are equal
the number a letter stands for
henry.example:
Worked example — already done. Not scored. PRETEND model. Not the game. Not NASA.
Rule: distance = 4 × minutes. Needed distance: 20.
Equation: 20 = 4 × t. Inverse of ×4 is ÷4, so t = 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
Check: 4 × 5 = 20. Both sides match.
worksheet:
Fractions. PRETEND model. One sample tray is the whole. Rocks fill 3/4. Dust fills 1/6. Hint: 3/4 = 9/12 and 1/6 = 2/12.
a) Fraction filled: ______
b) Fraction still empty: ______
c) Which is smaller, the empty part or 1/8? ______   Show the comparison.

Long division. PRETEND model. 2,354 bolts go into boxes that hold 27 bolts.
Full boxes: ______   Bolts left over: ______
Show the division in the box.

Algebra bridge. PRETEND model rule: distance = 15 × minutes + 12. The team needs distance 132. Let m stand for minutes.
a) Equation: 132 = 15 × m + 12
b) Undo +12, then undo ×15. m = ______
c) Check: 15 × ____ + 12 = ______
henry.challenge: Stretch, not required. Two pretend rovers work the same number of hours, h. Rover A collects 4 × h samples. Rover B collects 4 × h + 5 samples. Together they collect 45 samples. Find h, then check both rules. These are still pretend model numbers.

parentKey.assess: Score problems 1–3 only. The example is teaching. Reading checks are a warm-up, not the math score. The challenge is optional. Full credit needs the work, not only a final number. 5 = all three correct with work. 4 = one slip with the method mostly right. 3 = about half. 2 = a real try. 1 = needs another pass.

items.a:
a) 3/4 + 1/6 = 9/12 + 2/12 = 11/12 filled.
b) 1 − 11/12 = 1/12 empty.
c) The empty part, 1/12, is smaller than 1/8. Common denominator 24: 1/12 = 2/24 and 1/8 = 3/24. 2/24 < 3/24. (One twelfth is a smaller piece than one eighth.)

87 full boxes, remainder 5 bolts.
27 into 235 is 8, because 27 × 8 = 216. 235 − 216 = 19. Bring down 4 to make 194. 27 × 7 = 189. 194 − 189 = 5.
Check: 27 × 87 = 2,349, and 2,349 + 5 = 2,354.

Subtract 12: 120 = 15 × m. Divide by 15: m = 8 minutes.
Check: 15 × 8 + 12 = 120 + 12 = 132. Both sides equal.

frankie.title: Rocket Count-On 🚀
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud. Rockets count, and one number is hiding. About 14 minutes. No game today.
worksheet:
Count on. Circle the sum.
6 + 3 = 8   9   10

The unknown hides. Circle it.
5 + ____ = 9
3   4   6

Sound it out. Draw a line.
sun   red   hop
🐇   🔴   ☀️
Circle every see: I see the sun. I see a hop.

Trace: I see the sun.
Stretch: Write sun by yourself:

parentKey.assess: Score the worksheet. 5 = count-on, the missing addend, the comparison, and the word match are right, and he traced. Writing sun alone is the stretch, not required for a 5. Reading is supported by you.

items.a: sun → ☀️, red → 🔴, hop → 🐇. He should circle both see words. Stretch spelling: sun.
